title: Interaction Contracts & Launch Sentinel for Hosted Endpoints
creator: Ava Martinez
description: This ticket defines explicit interaction contracts across the hosted endpoint family (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) and a launch 'sentinel' checklist that gates release. The goal is to reduce ambiguity between product, SDKs, runtime, and ops so we can ship a consistent, testable, observable hosted surface with clear rollback conditions.
background: We have multiple PRDs and readiness checklists for individual hosted features; this PRD codifies cross-cutting behavior expectations (timeouts, deterministic fallback, error taxonomy, prefix/cache semantics, token accounting) and ties them to specific acceptance tests and runbook items. Past launches revealed edgecases around deterministic rerank scoring, embedding vector length mismatches, and chat KV cache invalidations during rollout.
goals: Define interaction contracts (request/response invariants, error classes, performance SLOs) for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank
Provide a minimal test harness and automated acceptance tests that runtime and SDK teams can run on every candidate release
Create a launch sentinel (gate checklist) that includes quality/regression signals, canary rollout plan, and rollback triggers
scope_in: Behavioral contracts for hosted API payloads (fields that are stable, optional, or experimental)
Acceptance test definitions and example fixtures for each endpoint type
Launch sentinel checklist items: metrics, smoke tests, canary schedule, docs, SDK compatibility, billing visibility
Operator runbooks for common regressions (rerank score drift, embedding dimensional mismatch, chat kv-staleness)
scope_out: Full rewrite of SDKs; only compatibility tests and upgrade notes will be included
Model architecture design or retraining work
assumptions: Runtime provides per-request metadata and stable request ids for tracing
Telemetry platform supports per-endpoint token counts, p50/p95 latency and error breakdowns
SDK teams will run acceptance tests in CI and report pass/fail prior to release
requirements: Canonical request/response JSON schemas for chat, completions, embeddings, rerank (versioned)
Mandatory fields and deprecation rules documented and machine-parseable
Per-endpoint acceptance tests (unit + integration) that execute against staging runtime
Quality thresholds: p95 latency <= 450ms for gen endpoints on hosted-small, error rate < 0.5% for steady traffic slices
Deterministic fallback policy: when a primary model is unavailable, system must return a documented placeholder response, log, and fallback to compatible variant with <= 10% perf degradation
Embeddings must include vector length in response metadata and fail with a clear 400 if client-specified vector dims mismatch
Rerank responses must include stable score normalization and rejection mode for out-of-range inputs
Chat must document prefix/KV cache semantics: which fields are cached, cache invalidation signals, and TTL defaults
api_contract_examples: Chat request: {"messages": [ {"role":"user","content":"..." } ], "conversation_id": "uuid" } -> response includes conversation_id, message_id, model_version, deterministic_seed(optional)
Completions: include truncated flag and token_count breakdown in response metadata
Embeddings: response must include vector_length and model_vector_id; if dims mismatch return 400 with code 'EMB_DIM_MISMATCH'
Rerank: response includes normalized_scores (0..1), original_index mapping, and a signed schema version
acceptance_criteria: All canonical JSON schemas checked into repo and referenced by SDKs
Automated acceptance test suite passes on staging with flaky rate < 0.5% for 72h
Performance: p50/p95 within agreed SLOs for each endpoint on the hosted-small profile
Telemetry: token-level cost, per-route latency, and error breakdowns visible in Console dashboards for staging and will populate within 15 minutes of traffic
Docs: Public API docs updated with behavior notes, deprecation schedule, and example failure modes
SDK compatibility: Node/Python SDKs pass integration tests against staging and include client-side validation for required fields
Runbooks: ops runbook created with run/rollback steps and at least one simulated incident run-through recorded
Canary: initial canary slice executed with canary_metrics within thresholds for 6 hours before 20% ramp
launch_checklist: Pre-cutover: schema and acceptance tests merged; no unresolved blockers
Telemetry: verify Console shows indicator panels for token_cost, p95_latency, error_rate
Evals: run a small eval suite (representative prompts) and compare logits/rerank scores to baseline; regression < 2% weighted
SDK: release patch with compatibility checks and client validation; publish changelog
Docs: publish endpoint behavior guide, migration notes for deprecated fields, and examples for error handling
Canary plan: 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 24h with automated rollback criteria configured
Alerting: set alerts for error/increase in token_cost > 25% and p95 latency degradation > 40%
Billing: verify per-route metering and invoice preview updated
Post-launch: 72-hour monitoring window, daily triage, and evaluation of quality signals
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Rerank score drift after kernel changes. Mitigation: include synthetic rerank test that verifies top-5 ranking fidelity and alerts on drift
Risk: Embedding dimension mismatch for downstream similarity stores. Mitigation: include strict validation in API and migration tooling for existing vectors
Risk: Unexpected latency regression from batching changes. Mitigation: run controlled perf experiments with golden traces and block rollout if p95 degrades > 40%
Risk: Docs/SDK mismatch. Mitigation: require SDK compatibility test as blocking merge for API schema changes
dependencies: ENG-75421: runtime: expose request_id and model_version in responses
ENG-76890: telemetry: per-endpoint token accounting pipeline
ENG-78102: SDK: client-side validation helpers for required fields
PM-331101: evals baseline and regression harness
notes: This PRD focuses on the behavioral surface visible to customers; internal runtime knobs (quantization, kernel selection) will be covered in related ENG tickets
We intentionally define conservative fallback behaviors to avoid silent correctness regressions during capacity pressure
Acceptance thresholds are intentionally tight for p95 latency to prioritize user-perceived experience for interactive applications
